elements.element: Customer has no obligation to purchase a minimum quantity or value of Services.
elements.evidence: The operative clause states that “Customer has no minimum purchase or take-or-pay commitment.”

elements.element: Fees are payable only for Services ordered by Customer or actually used by Customer.
elements.evidence: The operative clause states that Customer “owes Fees only for Services ordered by Customer under an Order Form or actually used by Customer.”

elements.element: Any commitment is limited to the current 12-month term and does not extend into later terms.
elements.evidence: The clause affirmatively eliminates all minimum purchase and take-or-pay commitments, so the condition under which a commitment-duration limit would be required is demonstrably absent.

elements.element: Customer may reduce any commitment on 30 days' notice.
elements.evidence: The clause affirmatively eliminates all minimum purchase and take-or-pay commitments, so there is no commitment requiring a reduction right.

elements.element: Any commitment shortfall is addressed through a true-up rather than a penalty.
elements.evidence: The clause affirmatively eliminates all minimum purchase and take-or-pay commitments and permits Fees only for ordered or actually used Services, so no commitment shortfall or associated penalty can arise.

result.reason: The operative redline fully implements the preferred position by eliminating minimum-purchase and take-or-pay obligations and limiting Fees to ordered or actually used Services. Because no commitment remains, each conditional fallback protection is also satisfied by the demonstrable absence of its triggering condition. The revision is focused on the offending commitment and introduces no unrelated obligation or contradiction.
